title: JNI Boundaries, References, Threads, and Exceptions

scout.purpose: Master jni boundaries, references, threads, and exceptions through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend jni boundaries, references, threads, and exceptions.

blocks.text: JNI bridges ART-managed Kotlin or Java and native code. Keep the boundary narrow, coarse-grained, and typed because marshalling, lifetime, exceptions, strings, arrays, and callbacks create complexity. JNIEnv is thread-local and must not be cached across threads. Native threads attach to the VM before JNI use and detach before exit. Local references are scoped to a native call or frame; global references survive until deletion and can retain entire managed graphs.

blocks.text: Cache class and method IDs safely with the correct defining class loader. A pending Java exception changes what JNI operations are legal; check, translate, or return rather than continuing blindly. Modified UTF-8 differs from arbitrary UTF-8. Avoid asynchronous ping-pong across the boundary and never call UI objects from arbitrary native threads. Keep ownership explicit for pinned arrays, direct buffers, native handles, callbacks, cancellation, and process shutdown. CheckJNI catches many contract violations during development.

blocks.text: Test with CheckJNI, stress threads, forced exceptions, class-loader variation, process recreation, and sanitizers. Inspect JNI global references and native memory. Fuzz native inputs before they reach privileged libraries. R8 rules must preserve dynamically resolved entry points, but RegisterNatives can reduce fragile name lookup. Treat native crashes as process crashes, retain exact symbols and build IDs, and make operations idempotent or transactionally safe across abrupt termination.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

blocks.title: Expert trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Caching JNIEnv in a global and using it from worker threads violates its thread affinity and can corrupt runtime interaction.

trap_check.mistake: Caching JNIEnv in a global and using it from worker threads violates its thread affinity and can corrupt runtime interaction.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Design a JNI engine boundary with explicit handles, thread attachment, references, exceptions, cancellation, R8, CheckJNI, fuzzing, and process-death recovery.

recall.prompt: What must a native-created thread do before using JNI?
recall.answer: Attach to the JavaVM to obtain its own JNIEnv, then detach before the thread terminates.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
